case_name: Thoti Manohar v State of Andhra Pradesh
respondent:
State of Andhra Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

15  May  2012
Cr.A. No. 1739 of 2007
The Judgment was delivered by : Dipak Misra, J.
1.  The present appeal, by special leave u/art. 136 of the Constitution of India, is directed against the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 6.3.2007 passed by the High Court of Judicature, Andhra Pradesh at Hyderabad in Criminal Appeal No. 603 of 2005 whereby the Division Bench of the High Court partly allowed the appeal by acquitting the accused No. 3 (A-3), namely, Thoti Sivaram, for the offence punishable u/s. 302 read with S. 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short 'the IPC') but maintained the conviction and sentence in respect of other offences as had been imposed by the learned Sessions Judge, Chittoor in Sessions Case No. 108 of 2003. Be it noted, the accused No. 1 (A-1) was convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 452, 302, 326 and 324 of the IPC, the accused No. 2 (A-2) was found guilty of the of
facts: A-1 and A-2 are real brothers and A-3 is their cousin.

The deceased, his brother Damodaran and other family members had an apprehension that if Dhanamma continued such kind of intimacy with A-1, she would not be in a position to perform the marriage of her daughter.
On 24.9.2002 at about 3.00 p.m., A-1 and A-2 drove their cows again for grazing the crop of the deceased.

On 25.9.2002, at about 11.00 a.m., when Sekhar, the deceased and Jayamma, wife of the deceased (PW-3), were in their house, A-1 and A-3 armed with iron rods and A-2 armed with billhook trespassed into the house of the deceased.
The prosecution, to establish the charges against the accused persons, examined 20 witnesses, exhibited 23 documents, namely, Exh. P-1 to P-23 and got MOs-1 to 9 marked.
issues: Whether the prosecution had been able to establish the charge u/s. 452 of the IPC against A-1 to A-3?
Whether the offence u/s. 302 of the IPC was proven against A-1?
Whether there was a common intention to extinguish the life spark of the deceased between A-2 and A-3?
petitioner_arguments: The learned trial Judge has grossly erred by placing reliance on the evidence of PWs-1 to 8, 10 and 12 despite the incurable discrepancies pertaining to the place and time of occurrence.
There was no circumstance on record to come to a definite conclusion that A-2 and A-3 shared a common intention with A-1 to do away with the life of the deceased.
respondent_arguments: A-2 and A-3 came armed with deadly weapons to the house of the deceased and dragged him from his house and attacked him.

They had earlier threatened the deceased with dire consequences and thus, the cumulative effect of the circumstances would go a long way to reveal that there was a common intention to extinguish the life spark of the deceased.
court_reasoning: The learned Sessions Judge appreciated the evidence of PW-1, Sekhar, the informant, PW-2, Rukmanamma, wife of Arunachalam, PW-3, Jayamma, mother of PW-1, PW-4 Parganam, PW-5, Damodaran and PW-6, Arunachalam, the injured eye witnesses who had supported the factum of assault on the deceased as well as on them; relied on the testimony of Gunasekhar, PW-7, S. Suri, PW8, and the then Circle Inspector of Police, PW-20, who conducted the investigation to accept the reliability of seizure of weapons in accordance with S. 27 of the Evidence Act.
holding: The Supreme Court upheld the conviction and sentence of the accused persons.
